page_title: Voicely — Offline Dictation & Call Transcription for Mac

summary.name: Voicely
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source macOS app for offline dictation, call recording transcription, and local audio/video file transcription, with output usable by AI agents like Claude Code and Cursor.
use_cases: Dictating text at the cursor in any Mac app
Recording and transcribing calls with speaker labels
Transcribing local audio or video files such as interviews
Giving spoken context to Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor
Keeping dictation and transcripts private on-device
summary.what_it_does: Voicely starts and stops dictation with a keyboard shortcut (⌥ + space) and transcribes speech locally, inserting clean text at the cursor in any app. It can record call or room audio and transcribe it with speaker diarization when available. It also transcribes dropped audio or video files locally using the Parakeet V3 model. Transcripts can be saved as files and exposed through a CLI and MCP server so AI agents can read them.
notable: Open source under the MIT license, no account or subscription
Runs on-device on the Neural Engine with Parakeet V3 (about 470 MB one-time model download)
CLI and MCP server let Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Hermes read saved transcripts
Speaker diarization for recorded calls when available
caveats: Mac only: requires macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon; no Windows, iOS, or Android version
First launch requires a roughly 470 MB speech model download and Microphone, Accessibility, and Screen Recording permissions (the last only when recording calls)
Speaker diarization is applied only 'when available'
